headline: Wall Street opens split: tech bounces on Nvidia, metals keep breaking as hike bets build
tone: Mixed, with a defensive core: the US open has not reset the day. Tech buyers are back after Nvidia's beat, but the metals rout has deepened and spread into miners on both sides of the Atlantic, which says the market is still pricing a hawkish Fed rather than a growth scare.
body: The Nasdaq is leading because Nvidia's numbers (Q3 revenue reported at about $115.8 billion, roughly double a year ago) gave chip buyers a reason to return after the post-Huang sell-off. The Dow lags on value and resource names, so this is a rotation back into AI hardware, not a broad bid.

The 14:30 data did little to steady rates: October housing starts jumped about 10% on a multifamily surge, but permits fell 7.4% and single-family permits are at a near two-year low with mortgage rates around 7.35%. That points to a softer housing pipeline, yet not enough to talk the Fed out of a December hike.

Metals are the day's real story. Gold has broken to its lowest since September 2025 and the selling has spread from bullion into copper and the gold and copper miners, including the Lundin names, as the strong dollar and hike bets raise the cost of holding them. Reports that Stanley Druckenmiller's firm has no equity exposure and has exited copper holdings add to the sense of de-risking in commodity-linked trades.

What would change the tone: tonight's FOMC minutes (20:00 Zurich) from the October hold, where two members voted to hike. A hawkish read would extend the dollar and metals moves and test whether the tech bounce holds into the close; a softer read is the one thing that could stop the metals slide and broaden the rally.

views.text: The open confirms the Nvidia beat is lifting hardware, but its halt to Hopper shipments to China and the unresolved CEO search keep it a trade rather than a re-rating. Miners are where the pain sits: they are carrying both lower metal prices and the de-risking flow.

Crude stays heavy after the US stock build and a sharp fall in US refining margins, which is easing pump prices and, at the margin, inflation pressure. TTF is easing too, but low European storage still sets the winter floor; Hormuz headlines remain the upside risk.
